parts:
Greetings Phil and others,

I fit a 16 item unidimensional model with a mix of 2PL and 2PLNRM items.  when I call coef(fit, simplify = T, IRTpars = T) I get the following error and warning:

Error in dimnames(x) <- dn : 
  length of 'dimnames' [2] not equal to array extent
In addition: Warning message:
In matrix(c(object@ParObjects$pars[[i]]@par, object@ParObjects$pars[[i]]@par -  :
  data length [8] is not a sub-multiple or multiple of the number of rows [3]

If I ask for slope - intercept rather than IRT parameters it prints the table with no error.  I've tried to pinpoint whether there is a particular offending variable, but have not found one.  when i run a traceback i get the error occurred at:

4. `colnames<-`(`*tmp*`, value = object@ParObjects$pars[[i]]@parnames)

The model has displayed without problems before. It began when i upgraded to R v. 3.5.1, so I'm hoping someone can help.

Here is my code:

know.num <- know.df %>% 
      dplyr::select(contains("know")) %>%
      mutate_all(funs(as.numeric(as.factor(.)))) 

#Collapse "incorrect" n<20 cells with "don't know" responses
n_less20 <- apply(know.num, 2, function(x) sum(x == 3, na.rm = T) < 20)

know.num <- know.num %>% 
      mutate_if(n_less20 == TRUE, funs(ifelse(. == 1, 1, 0))) %>%
      mutate_at(vars(know3.factor, know21.factor), funs(ifelse(. == 1, 1, 0)))

#Select out variables eliminated due to LD or low discrimination
know.num.red <- know.num %>% 
      dplyr::select(
            -c(know7.factor,
               know9.factor,
               know10.factor, 
               know17.factor,

Sorry, of course should have included a reproducible example.  Please see below.  Also it prints fine if mirt is called with SE=FALSE.  I've opened an issue on Github.  

Example:
#create data 
set.seed(4321)
a <- matrix(rep(1, 16))

d <- runif(16, -2.5, 2.5)

d0 <- c(rep(NA, 7), rep(0, 9))

d1 <- c(rep(NA, 7), runif(9, -2, 2))

intercepts <- matrix(c(d, d0, d1), ncol = 3)
            
ak <- rep(NA, 16)

ak0 <- c(rep(NA, 7), rep(0, 9))
         
ak1 <- c(rep(NA, 7), rep(1, 9))

nominal <- matrix(c(ak, ak0, ak1), ncol = 3)

items <- c(rep("2PL", 7), rep("2PLNRM", 9))

df <- simdata(a, intercepts, 591, itemtype = c(rep("2PL", 7), rep("2PLNRM", 9)), 
              nominal = nominal)

#Fit model with SE = T, poduces error.          
mod.se <- mirt(df, 1, 
             itemtype = c(rep("2PL", 7), rep("2PLNRM", 9)), 
             key = c(rep(NA, 7), rep(0, 9)),
             SE = T)
